name: radio-button
purpose: Atomic exclusive-choice control only — the circular radio input from Figma (no label, description, or helper). Wrap it in a horizontal `Field`, or a `Field.Label` choice card, for labeled layouts.
useWhen: One choice from a small set of mutually exclusive options whose labels are laid out separately (a table row, a custom option row).
A custom radio layout that the horizontal `Field` and the `Field.Label` choice card do not cover.
avoidWhen: A radio option in a form that needs its own label, description, or helper text → wrap it in a horizontal `field` (`Field orientation="horizontal"` + `Field.Content`).
Options that need visual weight, such as plans or tiers → use a `field` choice card (`Field.Label` wrapping a horizontal `Field`), or `radio-cards` for a horizontal grid of cards.
More than one option may be selected → use `checkbox`.
The options are many or loaded from data → use `select`.
related: field` — a horizontal `Field` puts the radio beside its label and description (the default inside forms); a `Field.Label` wrapping it is a card-style option with a selected border and background. Group the options in `Field.Set` + `Field.Legend`.
radio-cards` — horizontal grid of selectable cards with its own model.
select` — single choice from a dropdown when the options do not fit inline.
bestPractices: Bind every radio in a group to the same `v-model` and give them the same `name`; each one emits its own `value` when selected.
value` and `modelValue` are strings; map numeric or object ids to strings before binding.
Give each radio an accessible name: point a `label` element's `for` at `inputId`, or pass `aria-label`.
Wrap the group in a `fieldset` with a `legend` so the question itself is announced.

props.name: value
props.doc: Option value for this radio instance.

props.name: name
props.doc: HTML name shared across a mutually exclusive group.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Disables interaction and applies disabled tokens.

props.name: inputId
props.doc: id for the native input; links label to control.

examples.name: Default
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import RadioButton from '@aziontech/webkit/radio-button'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const selected = ref('')
</script>

<template>
  <RadioButton
    v-model="selected"
    name="webkit-radio"
    value="a"
    input-id="webkit-radio-a"
    aria-label="Option A"
  />
</template>

examples.name: Disabled
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import RadioButton from '@aziontech/webkit/radio-button'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const selected = ref('a')
</script>

<template>
  <fieldset class="flex items-center gap-(--spacing-4) border-0 p-0 m-0">
    <RadioButton
      v-model="selected"
      name="webkit-radio-disabled"
      value="a"
      disabled
      input-id="webkit-radio-disabled-a"
      aria-label="Disabled selected"
    />
    <RadioButton
      v-model="selected"
      name="webkit-radio-disabled"
      value="b"
      disabled
      input-id="webkit-radio-disabled-b"
      aria-label="Disabled unselected"
    />
  </fieldset>
</template>
